campaign: Hatchet-derived workflow contracts: durable attempts, declared capacity, keyed admission and conditional plan rows on existing Go owners
doctrine: Work and commit only in the overgo_hatchet worktree; do not push. docs/hatchet_for_overgo.md is the design record for this campaign and names, for every element, the observed Hatchet mechanism, the Overgo gap, the contract, the owner and the acceptance. No Hatchet source is copied, translated or vendored; every element is a contract restated on the existing Go owner that holds the neighbouring authority, and no parallel runtime, queue or expression language is added. Each row's verify names one acceptance test in the owning package guarded by the test file's existence; the acceptance names are planned work, not claims that the tests exist, and a row closes only when its named test executes and passes through the gate. Host rows land first; device tests are limited to eviction on the real device and the load lane's measured run, and a device verify carries its own OVERGO_CUDA_TEST and OVERGO_DATA_ROOT bindings. The lane cycle, in this order and repeated: merge current master into the lane except master's docs/plan.json, which never enters the lane; update this plan from the merged repository and its measured performance; execute the dispatched row; commit through the gate. Do not chase master during a row. One writer owns a plan edit and gates it. Findings outside the dispatched row are parked with cmd/finding, not folded in. Rows are ranked by their expected reduction of automation cost and their gain in development pace: gate wall per accepted row, re-executed work after interruption, and rows dispatched without operator intervention come before request-level admission, observability and serving measurement; a row's outcome records the measured change in those quantities. Audit language in code, evidence and commit messages is objective. Every element records the measurement that decides it: restart re-execution count, gate cost per accepted checkpoint, device idle time during host phases, and queued-to-first-token latency at declared concurrency; a row whose measurement shows no gain closes with that outcome recorded. Master paused development on 2026-09-06; this lane is the active development line. Gate mechanisms that master's paused validation-batch-control row also named, namely accepted-checkpoint evidence reuse across gate runs, gate wall per accepted checkpoint, and a host-wide exclusive device claim across worktrees and stores, are implemented here on the existing gate and loop owners, additively and minimally, so the later lane-to-master merge stays small; master's uncommitted work is never imported. Rows that subdivide declare a verification batch with a flush declaration of their own, so the campaign measures the mechanism it ships. Owner review 2026-09-06 ranks the gate work: reuse that a process kill can lose is not reuse, so every terminal success persists before the next check runs; a memo input covers every command of a verifier or the verifier is not cached; timing establishes expense while counterexamples establish selection safety, and both obligations stay separate; a flush declaration becomes a durable deferred obligation with governed promotion before it counts as batching; a skipped or cancelled row never satisfies a dependency that requires successful evidence unless that dependency declares it accepts the refusal; a progress refresh extends liveness only under an absolute budget ceiling that an operator budget always bounds. Rows follow that order: persistence, complete identities, shadow verification, physical device exclusion, governed promotion, then conditional workflows, placement and scheduling.

items.title: Diagnose and replay one plan row from its records

steps.title: Replay one attempt from its receipt with the same or new inputs
steps.rationale: A recorded attempt is re-run from its receipt under a new invocation count, reading memoised results where the inputs are unchanged and executing where they differ, which is the replay reference an agent uses after a diagnosis.

items.title: Declare slot cost, lane labels and sticky assignment on the existing schedulers

steps.title: Declare slot cost in device and host units on rows and operations, and labels with capacity on lanes
steps.rationale: Design record E3. plan.Resources becomes the declaration the scheduler charges: a row reserves its cost on one lane, a lane declares labels and capacity, and a required label that no lane holds leaves the row waiting with that reason.

steps.title: Assign by required labels, order by weight, break ties round-robin, and keep dependent rows sticky to the lane holding their resident model
steps.rationale: The locality scheduler already filters lanes on artifact locality; it gains weight ordering, round-robin ties and soft or hard sticky modes so that rows reusing one resident session are assigned by declaration rather than by hand.

steps.title: Express exclusive device rows as full device cost over the host-wide claim and admit host rows beside them
steps.rationale: A device row's cost equals the lane's device capacity and its admission takes the host-wide claim. The driver proves host-only rows dispatch beside an exclusive device row and a second device row waits with the claim holder recorded.

items.title: Evict waiting sessions by declared policy and release device claims after the device phase

steps.title: Declare TTL, capacity and priority eviction on resident session leases and waiting operations
steps.rationale: Design record E2. The ModelSessionDirector evicts by policy when an admission needs capacity: after a waiting TTL, under capacity pressure when permitted, and in priority order among candidates, recording the reason. A fake capacity model proves the order without a device.

steps.title: Release the device claim after the device phase while the host phase continues under the same attempt
steps.rationale: A row that generates on the device and scores on the host holds the device through scoring today. Release is a recorded transition; the claim cannot be reacquired without a new admission; the host phase completes under the same attempt identity.

steps.title: Evict and resume a resident session on the real device within the retained-memory bound
steps.rationale: The device measurement that decides E2: a second admission evicts a waiting resident session under memory pressure, the evicted session resumes by replay, and retained device memory stays within the bound the long-form guard records. Device idle time during the host phase is recorded before and after release.

items.title: Admit requests by declared key with recorded strategies and idempotency holds

steps.title: Derive a group key from declared request facts and apply round-robin, cancel-in-progress, cancel-newest and cancel-queued-except-newest strategies
steps.rationale: Design record E4. A new turn in the same conversation supersedes the in-flight one, one served model is shared fairly across users by a declared limit, and every cancellation records its reason. The key is derived from the conversation, model or workspace identity the request already carries.

steps.title: Coalesce queued model swaps to the newest request per endpoint and drain with recorded reasons
steps.rationale: The swap supervisor drains by a grace period today. Cancel-queued-except-newest applied to swap requests keeps only the latest requested model per endpoint and records why the superseded requests were dropped.

steps.title: Hold one in-flight automation run per idempotency key with a fallback TTL
steps.rationale: A duplicate webhook or schedule trigger with the same key collides while the owning run is not terminal and is admitted once it is; the fallback TTL bounds a key whose run never reaches a terminal state.

items.title: Record cancellation reasons and publish queue statistics per key

steps.title: Record a typed cancellation reason on every cancelled operation and row
steps.rationale: Design record E9. Schedule timeout, execution timeout, superseded by key, evicted, operator stop and dependency cancelled are the closed reasons; a cancellation without one is refused.

steps.title: Publish queued and running counts with oldest age per key for operations and lanes
steps.rationale: The front page and the lane dispatcher read the same statistics: counts per state, the distribution per key, and the age of the oldest queued item, derived from operation records rather than from logs.

items.title: Pause one automation with declared behaviour for its due slots

steps.title: Pause one automation with queue-or-drop behaviour for due schedule slots and a queue TTL
steps.rationale: Design record E8. In-flight runs continue, new runs queue under a TTL or the due slot is dropped as declared, expired queued runs cancel with the reason recorded, and unpausing requeues the rest. The recorded operator stop remains the whole-plan pause.

items.title: Measure serving under concurrent load and ratchet its floors

steps.title: Add a load lane that drives the served model at declared concurrency and collects timings with bounded fetch concurrency and a pending TTL
steps.rationale: Design record E10. Queued-to-first-token latency and throughput through the swap proxy are unmeasured. The collector fetches run timings concurrently under a bound and abandons a run whose timings never arrive after a TTL, so a broken run cannot stall the lane.

steps.title: Publish one measured load run and ratchet latency and throughput floors from it
steps.verify: test -f cmd/load-lane/floors_windows_test.go && OVERGO_CUDA_TEST=1 OVERGO_DATA_ROOT=C:/Users/jeffm/overgo go test ./cmd/load-lane -run '^TestServingLoadFloors$' -count=1 -timeout=15m
steps.rationale: The first floors are the measured values of the smallest served text model at the declared concurrency; later runs may only tighten them, as the clone baseline ratchets. The record binds the model, recipe, concurrency and inference surface.

items.title: Publish the measurements that decide the campaign and record the workflow contracts in the README

steps.title: Publish restart re-execution, gate cost per checkpoint, device idle during host phases and load floors before and after, and document the adopted contracts
steps.rationale: The closeout binds each element to its recorded measurement, records the elements that showed no gain with their outcome, and updates the README's workflow sections to describe the contracts as they exist. It depends on every terminal row.

verification_batch.rationale: The closeout's four measurements are independent acceptances that accumulate under the campaign's own flush declaration.
verification_batch.reopen_when: Any measured element is re-run or a measurement owner changes.

Reuse historical fixed-budget controls and long-form records only after an exact source/surface and protocol independence check; the raw-continuation ladder alone does not satisfy the three fixed-budget controls. Implement TestAcceptedE4BModalities in the existing compatibility owner as the final read-only join: reject any missing modality, protocol, task-quality assertion, source identity, completion denominator, resource check or unpromoted required binding. Store one evidence bundle for the model, then feed existing memory/benchmark/modality reports from those same records. Run the batch once at integration after related changes; scoped diagnostics during implementation are not completion. Master owns validation and numerical/admission repairs; GUI owns HTTP implementation, audio owns native streaming and training. No projector promotion until all declared media modes have evidence.

The producer prerequisite owns the CPU/GPU integration batch and the read-only final assertion. This row performs the clean-source measurement and evidence-binding phase: reuse exact proven-independent protocol/resource records, acquire missing or invalidated cells, then run the final read-only acceptance once. Do not repeat the producer batch for every record or report update. If measurement exposes a new runtime defect, stop affected measurement, retain the failed record, and bind one new coherent repair producer before resuming clean-source publication; never reopen a completed identity or waive source cleanliness. The audio merge already supplies step-local verification batches, exact subordinate completion/recovery evidence and independent per-package cache reuse. The remaining work is checkpoint commits without premature parent completion, durable outstanding obligations bound to cumulative changes, mandatory escalation and measured scheduling through the existing plan/gate/OvergoDB owners.

Implement a concrete governed checkpoint path in cmd/gate: record implemented versus verified versus promoted states without pruning the parent. Persist outstanding checks with exact cumulative source/fixture/environment identities, survive interruption/restart, reject orphaning through replan or branch changes, and require one complete final integration gate. Persistence, authentication, concurrency, kernels, public contracts and gate-policy changes immediately trigger their required checks; the controller may adjust scheduling only inside declared limits. Until this exists, full gates remain mandatory for commits. Batch related implementation by capability/dependency, not commit counts; narrower diagnostics do not grant promotion.

Report wall time by phase, independently reused packages, executed checks, outstanding obligations, failures found and invalidation causes. Use the recent GUI merge failures (1757.2s and 1137.7s after successful verification) and final 952.9s run as recorded before evidence for early refusal and scheduling efficiency; do not claim these wall times predict another model. The exclusive GPU lease finding evidence:sha256:0f4b6d07607b3fa8ee6ee7f320646e5dbbd5b38b025a19c2046d54aed7fa4b4e remains open: consumers must enforce admitted resources before isolated measurements. Classify those by affected required acceptance versus optional/platform coverage: resolve every required missing fixture; record unsupported-platform exclusions with exact reasons and never count them as passing. steps.rationale: The E4B ladder reportedly grew from 14 GB loaded to 39 GB after rung 32768. items.title: Recover small-head decode throughput without losing long-context correctness

steps.title: Recover small-head decode throughput without losing long-context correctness
steps.rationale: The reviewed short-context Qwen2.5-0.5B rate fell from 295 to 139 tokens/s while E4B remained within about three percent. Keep split-key correctness, NLL and memory guarantees; recover the measured short-context gap within predeclared noise bounds without trading away larger-context throughput. Bind both kernel parity and end-to-end Qwen/E4B assertions. Remove capacity-wide work and redundant transfers before introducing another dispatch policy; retain one shared path wherever parity permits.
